result:
The proposed answer of 2/9 is probably wrong, but I can't verify the true value.

The cited bound "at least (2n−5)/9 vertex-disjoint P₃'s" is not a result I can confirm, and the solution gives no construction showing it is tight. The one thing I can check is an upper bound. Any P₃-packing uses 3 vertices per copy, so λ ≤ n/3 and c ≤ 1/3. That is consistent with 2/9 but does not establish it.

A natural construction gives ratio 1/3: take an independent set I, with each vertex of I placed in a face of a triangulated set S. Then every P₃ uses at least one vertex of S, so λ ≤ |S| = k, while n = 3k − 4, giving a ratio near 1/3. Reaching 2/9 would need a different blocking structure that wastes more vertices. I don't know of a verified construction doing that, and I recall the literature on P₃-packings in planar triangulations giving a bound with denominator 7 (around 2/7) rather than 9, but I am not certain of that recollection.

So I can't confirm 2/9 as the infimum, and the justification given for it appears unsupported.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 2
